r3_note: D3 and D8 paired two different moments: D3 = r2's 12:44 preposition row (r1's عشان يكون is D21); D8 = r2's 24:50 person row (r1's 25:08 b-drop is D22). بقيم (D9) is on Amal's sheet - the engine is right. 43:10 'صح، بس order. rows.medi_said: كيف كان الـ-- كيف كان العروسة؟ عروس؟
rows.why: He said bride (عروسة/عروس) for the wedding; she supplied عرس.
Letters swapped (زعمت for عزمت, sheet 'i invited | Ana 3azamet'); Amal recast and he confirmed at 04:05 'you corrected me'.

rows.medi_said: Sa alaat ila nun-- ila tult.
rows.why: For 1:40 he said talaat illa tult (2:40); Amal asked 'تلات أو تنتين؟' and he changed to Intayn ila tult. Could be she simply didn't hear - low.
rows.r3_why: Her either/or question names the right hour and he switches - a prompt. Clock time with illa = E2, not a vocab word slip.

rows.why: He said tonight (sheet: tonight | ellaile) for today and left out the weather word (sheet: hot (weather) | Shoab | شوب); right side is my reading.
rows.english: Today the weather is very very hot.
rows.r3_challenge: Amal's 'عن جد؟' reacts to a weather word (the AC then broke): the engine likely dropped شوب after جو; الليلة may also be the engine. Needs audio before scoring الليلة/missing شوب as his vocab slip.

rows.why: 'On YouTube' is 3ala (على اليوتيوب), not la-; Amal let it pass. Engine may have cut على.
rows.english: I watched a video on YouTube
rows.r3_why: Plausible preposition slip, let pass; low.

rows.why: Long aa inserted in صلّح (salaa7to); Amal recast صلحته, he repeated صلاhto - same kind as agreed A19 بزياد -> بزيد.
rows.r3_why: Voiced recast of a wrong form of a word he knows; treated as tier 2 like A19.

rows.medi_said: Is it raki? What was electricity?
rows.why: He asked for electricity; she supplied كهربا.

rows.medi_said: مهندس-- Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟
rows.amal_said: مهندس الكهربا. ... Or some people say كهربجي. It's easier.
rows.why: He asked how to say electrician; she taught the new word كهربجي (didn't-know, tier 0).
rows.r3_why: Transcript 09:00-09:28: a how-do-you-say question, she supplies كهربجي. Didn't-know, tier 0.

rows.why: He re-said her new word كهربجي as كراجي (twice, 09:30 and 09:39); Amal re-said كهـ، كهربجي stressing the lost syllable.
rows.r3_why: A garbled form of the word she just taught, voiced fix; not a single dropped ع/ط/ق, a whole syllable is missing.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، كهربجي، هو مهندس
rows.why: 'He is not an electrician' in the plain present takes مش before the noun, not ما يكون.
rows.english: He isn't an electrician, he's an engineer.

rows.medi_said: صلاح، صلاحني شوي. صلاحلي, helps to me, شوي.
rows.amal_said: صلحني would be he fixed me. ... You said صلح which is fix. did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: He used fix (صلح) for help; she explained صلحني = he fixed me and asked, he gave ساعدني.

rows.amal_said: صلحني would be he fixed me. Like you, you were who's being fixed. ... Fixed for me، صلح لي.
rows.why: Amal explained -ni makes 'fixed me'; 'for me' needs la- + ending (صلح لي).
rows.english: he fixed (it) for me a bit
rows.r3_why: Distinct from agreed A6 (vocab: صلح vs ساعد): here she named the object/preposition-ending rule. His صلاحلي at 10:40 came after her 10:30 صلح لي, so not a self-fix.

rows.why: بلوزة is feminine so the colour takes the feminine form; he took it right after her line ('وردنية that's right'); the engine garbled her word.
Wrong I-form past of ضل (sheet 'i stayed/kept | Ana dallait | أنا ضليت'); Amal asked what and recast ضليت.
rows.r3_why: He knows ضل (on her sheet, conjugated there); the slip is the past-tense I-ending of a doubled verb -> grammar B5, not a vocab non-word.

rows.medi_said: اه، this is take Allah بيتي.
rows.why: Wrong preposition before بيتي (engine wrote 'Allah', likely على); Amal prompted بِ أو فِي and he said بي بيتي.
rows.r3_why: r1's half (عشان يكون) is a separate slip ruled under D21; this ruling is r2's preposition row, which Amal prompted at 12:48.

rows.why: 'Because there is AC' needs في, not يكون (or عشان يكون في); Amal let it pass. My reading.
rows.r3_why: Real but unvoiced; low. This is r1's half of D3.

rows.why: وحدة (one) goes after the noun like an adjective; she recast كلمة وحدة.

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.why: Two of a noun uses the dual -ain (فعلين), not noun + تنين; Amal let it pass.
rows.r3_why: Real dual slip, let pass. E1 (number + noun: 2 has its own form) is the closer bucket; A9 as bucket2.

rows.why: 'I annoyed you' is زعجت + ك; he added -تي (the you-f ending); she recast زعجتك.
انزعج takes من (she said so at 14:35); he said ما, she asked 'why ما?', he fixed it to مني.
A how-do-you-say question with a guess; she supplied كمان واحد and he repeated (same treatment as the agreed A4 'Is it raki? What was electricity?').
rows.r3_why: Phrased as a question ('One more is ...?'), so a didn't-know: tier 0 / asked.

rows.why: With إنتي the adjective must be feminine; her question made him say مزعوجة.
The subject is 'many things' (plural) so the verb takes plural -و; she recast twice (again at 20:32).
rows.english: Many things annoy me these days.

rows.why: Singular يوم for 'these days'; Amal supplied the plural أيام (he: 'I even wrote أيام').
rows.r3_why: He knows أيام (wrote it himself); the fix is singular -> plural = A9 grammar, not a vocab tier-2 form.

rows.medi_said: إنتي متأكتي إلي إنتو ما ازعجتو
rows.why: 'sure that' needs إنو; اللي is 'the one that'; she said مش اللي.
rows.english: Are you sure that you didn't annoy him?

rows.why: Feminine of متأكد is متأكدة/mit2akkde; engine wrote متأكتي (-ti verb-like ending) - may be engine on mit2akde.
rows.r3_why: Plausible gender-ending slip, let pass; d->t is S4 so only the ending matters, which the engine may have garbled - low.

rows.why: 'You didn't annoy him' needs the object ending -ه on the verb; he left out 'him'.

rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: After إذا the verb keeps its b-; she recast بشوف and he took it (إذا ما بشوفك).
rows.english: if I don't see you happy

rows.why: Gave a positive command for 'don't be annoyed'; Amal prompted 'So don't be' and he said ما تنزعجي.
The person goes on the end of the preposition: منهم, not من + هم.
rows.r3_challenge: 'من هم' vs 'منهم' is only word spacing in the transcript; nothing audible marks it as wrong and Amal gave no signal - likely an engine split, not his error.

rows.why: 'It wasn't their intention' is past, so كان is needed (ما كان قصدهم) (my reading).
For 'they upset you' he used the you/she-form بتدايك; Amal re-said 'They upset you.' and he moved to the plural (ض->د is S4).
rows.r3_why: Two different moments: r1's 25:08 b-drop row is ruled under D22; this is r2's 24:50 person slip, prompted by her English 'They upset you.' (PG-22).

rows.why: After 'their intention (to)' the verb drops b-; Amal recast يدايقوكي (engine spelling), he kept بيتايوكي.
rows.r3_why: Voiced recast removing the b-; the ض/ق sounds are S4 only.

rows.medi_said: So I add his بزيء، بزياد،
rows.why: Wrong form of بزيد (I add); Amal recast.
He groped for 'remove' with non-words شول / فيل; she supplied بقيم (sheet 'i remove / take away | Ba2eem | بقيم' - engine is right, not بشيل); he echoed بعينك/بعيم.
rows.r3_why: Non-word attempts at a sheet word -> tier 1. بقيم is the real word (on her sheet), so r2's 'likely بشيل' reading is wrong.

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: In an idafa the first word takes no el-: أول الفعل / أول الكلمة; he put الـ on أول twice. He also uses 'الـ،' as a filler, so low.
rows.english: the beginning of the verb / word
rows.r3_why: Repeated twice with el- on the first word; Amal's 'Mm.' is no fix. Low because الـ is often his hesitation filler.

rows.why: بخسر (I lose) for بكسر (I break, sheet 'i get broken | Bankeser'); Amal: قريب. بكسر.
Plain present needs b-: بيكسروا; every other person in the same drill had b-. Engine may have dropped the b-.
rows.r3_why: Real-looking B1 miss in a conjugation drill, let pass; engine could have eaten the b-, so low.

rows.why: After بتضلي (engine بتزلي) he said the verb without its you-prefix t- (engine زري); he asked 'I say?' and Amal answered she didn't hear the t; he then said بتكسري.
rows.r3_why: Her echo shows the slip was the missing t- (person prefix). Engine garbled the word, so low.

rows.why: MSA -tum for you-plural past; spoken is -tu (he said كسرتوا right at 29:18); Amal let it pass. Engine may have normalised.
rows.r3_why: Plausible ending slip in a drill, let pass; low.

rows.why: 'His cups' needs the plural كاسات + ه; he said the singular (sheet 'cup | Kaasa | كاسة'); Amal recast the plural (engine wrote كساته).
rows.r3_why: Plural via the -aat ending is a buckets rule (A9), so grammar, not vocab tier 2.

rows.why: كاسة is feminine so the verb takes -ت; she recast and he said 'Oh, because it's female'.
The sentence was 'when she was 12'; he said 11, she supplied إتناش.
He added -a to مضارع; Amal answered with مضارع (voiced), he repeated المضارعة at 44:41 anyway.
rows.r3_why: Same slip at 44:33 and 44:41 - one row, the first. Her voiced مضارع right after is a soft recast; low.

rows.amal_said: You would use انكسر، بس my issue is with the verb itself ... It's physical.
rows.why: For the AC that stopped working she said كسر is physical breaking and the word is خربان / خرب.
rows.english: The AC broke (stopped working) from the heat.

rows.why: 'I have never broken anything' is past; she asked بكسر or كسرت and he said ما كسرت.

rows.why: He swapped letters in تبعي (mine) giving تعبي (tired me); she asked what he meant and he rephrased.
A verb is negated with ما before it, not مش; she recast ما نمت منيح and he took it.
He invented the plural فعلات; she supplied أفعال.

rows.medi_said: I am annoyed is أنا-- hold on. مزعج.
rows.why: مزعج = annoying, مزعوج = annoyed (sheet 'annoyed | Maz3ooj'); Amal's 'مم مم مم' came with his fix.
